subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Should OpenClaw accept a shared media-core/plugin-SDK filename decoding surface now, and what first-consumer scope is required before this issue can close?
rationale: Root policy keeps core lean, but this request crosses channel adapters and plugin boundaries; choosing media-core, plugin SDK, or channel-local ownership is a maintainer product/API decision, especially with a partial open PR already in flight.

options.title: Refresh the shared decoder path
options.body: Ask for or sponsor a refreshed PR that puts the decoder in the media-core/plugin-safe boundary and wires the first proven media and Feishu paths through it.

options.title: Keep narrow channel fixes only
options.body: Continue accepting targeted Feishu/media bug fixes and leave the multi-channel shared decoder for later evidence.

options.title: Defer the utility
options.body: Keep this issue open as design backlog until more non-Feishu channel failures prove the shared API surface is worth adding.

recommendation.title: Refresh the shared decoder path
recommendation.body: Ask for or sponsor a refreshed PR that puts the decoder in the media-core/plugin-safe boundary and wires the first proven media and Feishu paths through it.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history is the merged Feishu filename recovery and release-tag ownership around this media/channel boundary.
